page: Google Cloud Platform x4-1920-32t-metal is an ultra-dense bare-metal instance categorized under the memory-optimized family. The system is engineered around an x86_64 CPU architecture providing 1920 dedicated virtual CPUs. System memory totals 32768 GB (32 TB), which yields an extensive allocation of roughly 17.07 GB of RAM per processor core.

The hardware configuration omits discrete GPU acceleration, directing all host resources toward CPU processing and massive memory allocation. Local disk storage is not included on the platform, requiring system storage configurations to rely on external network-attached volumes. Furthermore, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating VPC routing configurations for network connectivity.

Operating on a bare-metal tier with 32 terabytes of memory allows extreme scale-up deployments within a single non-virtualized host environment. This physical profile reduces the communication latency and software overhead typically associated with scaling across distributed multi-node clusters. The substantial memory-to-core ratio delivers efficiency for memory-saturated environments, provided that the vast hardware resources are continuously utilized.

Given the magnitude of its compute and memory capabilities, Google Cloud Platform x4-1920-32t-metal is engineered for the most demanding enterprise infrastructure tasks. Appropriate deployments include massive in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, hyperscale distributed caching layers, high-throughput financial modeling engines, and monolithic batch transformation frameworks.
description: Google Cloud Platform x4-1920-32t-metal is an ultra-high-capacity bare-metal server belonging to the memory-optimized family. Additionally, it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its massive memory footprint and vast core allocation, the hardware profile is tailored specifically for resource-dense enterprise operations where maximum single-node memory addressability is critical. Cost efficiency is determined by consolidating multiple heavy workloads onto a single unified bare-metal host, minimizing multi-node clustering overhead. The configuration is directly suitable for hyper-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning platforms, extensive real-time analytical caches, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
